title: QUIC server-side 0-RTT admission anti-replay gate architecture
purpose: Define the internal server 0-RTT admission gate that composes validated PSK state, remembered transport-parameter acceptance, and listener-local one-time ticket consumption before any future server ZeroRtt opening or delivery path can use early data.
design_summary: The server 0-RTT admission decision is kept behind an internal gate instead of being inferred from successful resumption. The caller must provide an already validated PSK-binder result from the same managed listener ticket store. The gate then evaluates remembered transport parameters with the existing server 0-RTT transport-parameter policy and consumes the matching live ticket identity from the listener-local store exactly once. Replayed, unknown, expired, unvalidated-PSK, or transport-parameter-rejected attempts fail closed before any early data can be delivered. The normal resumption lookup path stays available for 1-RTT resumption. The slice deliberately keeps early_data ticket advertisement, server ZeroRtt packet opening, application delivery, public API changes, IsSupported widening, HTTP/3, external ticket persistence, and cluster-wide anti-replay coordination outside the support boundary.
edge_cases_and_constraints: PSK binder validation is a prerequisite input; this gate does not parse ClientHello or validate binders itself.
Transport-parameter rejection happens before ticket consumption so invalid parameter attempts do not burn a live ticket.
A live ticket identity can be consumed only once for early-data admission within the listener-local in-memory store.
Expired tickets are removed and cleared when an early-data admission attempt reaches the ticket-consumption step.
The normal live-ticket lookup path remains separate so the existing 1-RTT resumption proof is not weakened.
The gate is internal and does not advertise early_data, open server ZeroRtt packets, or deliver application data.
alternatives_considered: Treat accepted resumption PSK as sufficient for 0-RTT. Rejected because server early-data admission also needs remembered transport-parameter validation and anti-replay ownership.
Consume the ticket before transport-parameter validation. Rejected because parameter-rejected attempts should fail without burning unrelated live state.
Mark the interop zerortt cell supported once anti-replay state exists. Rejected because the server still does not advertise early_data, open ZeroRtt packets, or deliver early application data.
risks: Calling the gate before binder validation would make anti-replay state depend on unauthenticated input.
Sharing ticket state beyond one listener would imply persistence or cluster coordination that this slice does not implement.
Treating the internal gate as a runtime support claim would overstate zerortt readiness.
